subject: science
passage: In 2011, images from an orbiting spacecraft revealed dark streaks on Martian slopes that appear in warm seasons, lengthen gradually downhill, and fade when temperatures drop. Called recurring slope lineae, the streaks were widely interpreted as evidence of salty water seeping from the ground, a striking possibility given that liquid water is otherwise thought to be extremely scarce on the Martian surface.
passage_b: Planetary geologist Rhys Mbatha questions whether flowing water is needed to explain the streaks. Surveys of many sites show that the streaks end on slopes of nearly the same steepness at which loose, dry sand stops sliding, a pattern expected of grain flows but hard to explain if liquid were seeping from below. Mbatha allows that small amounts of moisture might help trigger the flows, but he argues that the streaks themselves are best explained as movements of dry material.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the interpretation in Text 1?

choices.A: By favoring dry grain flows as the cause while allowing moisture a minor role
choices.B: By rejecting the observation that the streaks change with the seasons
choices.C: By agreeing that the streaks are formed mainly by seeping salty water
choices.D: By arguing that moisture has no part at all in how the streaks form on Mars

explanation.why: Text 1 reports that the streaks were "widely interpreted" as signs of seeping salty water. Mbatha argues that they are "best explained as movements of dry material," because they stop at the steepness where dry sand stops sliding, though he "allows that small amounts of moisture might help trigger the flows." So he offers a different main explanation while leaving room for a little moisture.
explanation.A: Correct. Mbatha explains the streaks as dry grain flows but grants that moisture might help trigger them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 does not dispute the seasonal pattern; it disputes what causes the streaks.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Mbatha questions whether flowing water is needed and favors dry flows instead.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Mbatha allows that small amounts of moisture "might help trigger the flows," so he does not rule moisture out.
